choices.content: The number of combinations equals the number of permutations multiplied by \(k\)
The number of combinations equals the number of permutations divided by the factorial of \(k\)
The number of combinations equals the factorial of \(n\)

question.prompt: What is the relationship between \(C(n,k)\) and \(A(n,k)\)?

solutions.explanation: The elements within each combination have \(k!\) permutations, so \(C(n,k)=A(n,k)/k!\).
solutions.title: Count the orders of each selection
